claimScopes.authoredEvidence: BRCA1 and BRCA2 have different repair roles. Brca1-deficient mouse embryonic stem cells had impaired homologous repair of defined chromosome breaks in Moynahan 1999. claimScopes.authoredEvidence: A DNA lesion is a physical or chemical problem; a mutation is a lasting sequence change. Repair can remove damage before a mutation is fixed. Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. claimScopes.authoredEvidence: Repair capacity can change after treatment. In the selected eight-person resistant metastatic breast cancer cohort of Waks 2020, four acquired definite or putative BRCA reversions; other mechanisms could restore repair too. A reversion can restore a disrupted reading frame, while old genomic patterns remain. This selected cohort does not establish a common or most-frequent mechanism across all breast cancers, and a single tissue or blood sample can miss heterogeneous reversions.

Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.
